analysis: The code snippet calls `tables.toArray(new String[tables.size()])`. The `tables` set is declared as `Set<String>`, so all elements are of type String. The argument is a newly allocated array of type String[]. The `toArray` method's documentation (for Java's Set interface) declares two exceptions: ArrayStoreException and NullPointerException. NullPointerException is thrown if the specified array is null; here the array is created via `new String[tables.size()]`, which is never null, so this exception is avoided. ArrayStoreException is thrown if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in the set. Since the array is String[] and the elements are String (which are exactly the same type and String is a supertype of itself), the condition for this exception is not met; thus it is also avoided.
answer: Both declared exceptions (ArrayStoreException and NullPointerException) are avoided in the calling context.
remark: Since both exceptions are avoided (the array is non-null and its type is a supertype of all set elements), there is no trigger scenario for any exception in this code.
